pr_title: find module - stop dir traversal when depth is exceeded
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY

Empty the list used by os.walk when depth is exceeded rather than traverse the whole directory.
Fixes #73627

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

seems to have been caused by fdfa6fec75da14d7e145eccf7c092fba684ee1e2

The old (2.9) version would cull the dirs list (ie. `del(dirs[:])`) when depth had been reached, but the v2.10 code just does a continue, implying that os.walk() will continue to recurse into more dirs (and add the results to the 'looked' count, which should be a good way to verify this is happening).

Edit: so also related to https://github.com/ansible/ansible/commit/39b394204870fda6de789809a3d69f58da3e7c31#diff-2892d11343093d8d9569cb74bcb5a8e2e0b773c3bbf556387d70de131baf1228L417 which looks to be where the bug was actually added.

Edit2: That commit (https://github.com/ansible/ansible/commit/39b394204870fda6de789809a3d69f58da3e7c31) also changed directory-culling os.walk() semantics here: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/commit/39b394204870fda6de789809a3d69f58da3e7c31#diff-c3f1ae8c6250b3a6be1533094e8b19b6b3674a8d1b7d86794176ee47d224d67fL857-R857

Those seem to be the only 2 os.walk() dirs semantics changes at least, from a quick look.  That commit needs a more thorough audit, imo, for possibly other inadvertent bugs.

review_comments: [Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/datastructures.html) says that `del dirs[:]` is equivalent to `dirs.clear()`. Just out of curiosity is there a reason to use the former? Is it faster maybe?
`clear()` does not seem to exist in py2.7
